title: The Lucron Network: A Relational Pre-Geometric Framework for Spacetime, Quantum Mechanics, Gravity, and Cosmology
content: We propose the Lucron Model, a relational pre-geometric framework in which spacetime, matter, and gravity emerge from a network of identical fundamental units called Lucrons. The model is built on fifteen axioms that replace the continuum assumption of standard physics with a discrete, relational ontology. Lucrons have no intrinsic properties; all physical properties emerge from the relations (links) between them. Each link carries one bit of information and is characterized by three parameters: interaction weight \( w_L \), causal delay \( \tau_L \), and interaction range \( \ell_L \). A dictionary maps these parameters to macroscopic observables \( (\hbar, G, \Lambda) \). We derive the speed of light as\( c = \ell_L / \tau_{\text{step}} \), where \( \tau_{\text{step}} \) is the local QCA update time. We show that Lorentz invariance emerges statistically via the Sorkin-Malament theorem, with corrections of order \( (E/E_P)^2 \). The microdynamics is a quantum cellular automaton (QCA) that is exactly unitary and reversible; the Schr\"odinger equation emerges in the continuum limit. The nonlinear Schrödinger-Newton equation is shown to be an effective field-mean description. We identify the wave-particle duality with quantum gravity: a particle's own gravity causes it to diffuse into a wave, and measurement re-localizes it. Fermions are classified as topological knots in the network, with mass determined by the equilibrium size of the knot. The Standard Model gauge group \( SU(3) \times SU(2) \times U(1) \) emerges from the local structure of the network: triangular plaquettes with 3 binary links give \( SU(3) \), and digonal plaquettes with 2 binary links give \( SU(2) \times U(1) \). The universe undergoes a cyclic evolution: pure Lucrons contract into a minimal black hole (Big Bang), which evaporates into matter, antimatter, and dark matter; as black holes of increasing size evaporate, they produce pure Lucrons (dark energy), driving cosmic expansion. The matter-antimatter asymmetry is shown to be emergent, depending on the moment of expulsion from the Big Bang. The model makes several falsifiable predictions: a minimum black hole mass \( M_{\min} \approx 3 \times 10^{22} \) kg, a cosmological drift of the fine-structure constant \( |\dot{\alpha}/\alpha| \sim 10^{-18} \) yr\( ^{-1} \), Lorentz violation at Planck scale, no fourth generation of fermions, and a homogeneous CMB without inflation. We explicitly delineate the epistemic status of each result, distinguishing postulates, algebraic identities, qualitative mechanisms, and genuine predictions.
